tldr: For overlapping public groups, the worst-family cumulative Neyman regret is \(\mathcal R(T,M)\asymp T^{2/3}(\log M)^{1/3}\) uniformly for \(T\ge4\) and \(2\le M\le2^T\). A terminating shared-feedback assignment rule attains the upper bound on every bounded fixed potential-outcome table with arbitrary public contexts, without pointwise or prefix energy floors. A finite legal-table prior supplies the matching all-policy converse on the original comparison domain, where both floors remain imposed. For the specified subgroup IPW estimator, regret is exactly excess randomization variance multiplied by squared group size. The proof credits scalar reciprocal FTRL, sleeping aggregation, rare-arm testing, and IPW identities; the delivered result is the matched endpoint family frontier and its shared-information converse.
